**1 — Scene:** A main plate with two halves of a filled tortilla wrap and three salmon–avocado sushi pieces, with two small sauce cups alongside. I exclude the separate salad, soup, brownie and drink.

**2 — Vessel:** The main dinner plate appears about **26 cm** across: area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ **531 cm²**. Each sauce cup is approximately **4 cm** across: area ≈ **12.6 cm²**.

**3 — Items:** Chicken-and-vegetable tortilla wrap; salmon–avocado sushi; pale herb dressing; dark soy sauce. The wrap estimate includes its visible filling and any internal sauce.

**4–7 — Area, volume, weight and energy:**

| Item | Vessel area covered | Area × average height = gross volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| Three sushi pieces | 12% of plate | 64 cm² × 2.5 cm = 160 ml | 0.90 g/ml | 144 g | 155 | 223 kcal |
| Herb dressing | 90% of its cup | 11.3 cm² × 1.3 cm = 15 ml | 1.00 g/ml | 15 g | 400 | 60 kcal |
| Soy sauce | 90% of its cup | 11.3 cm² × 1.1 cm = 12 ml | 1.00 g/ml | 12 g | 50 | 6 kcal |

The main-plate food footprints total **38%** of the plate area; the remaining area is exposed plate. Heights describe average pile thickness, not the tallest point.

**8 — Sanity check:** About **481 g and 878 kcal** is plausible for a substantial wrap, three large sushi pieces and small amounts of sauce. Wrap filling and dressing composition are the largest energy uncertainties.
